proof:
# Integer-normal criticality with empty and full supporting facets

This is a finite-base extension of the local support-face calculation
in `candidate 568f7cf028ec23b6`.
It applies to full positive d-dimensional fibers, d>=2, and gives a
necessary condition only. It is not a mixed-depth lower bound.

Let P be the finite set of positive-volume integer bases of a compact
convex body. Fix a source (z0,y) and a through-source closed cap

    u.(x-y)+b.(z-z0)>=0,    u!=0.

Assume this cap is locally minimizing in all integer-normal tilts b
with u and the source fixed. Write p_z=z-z0 and t_z=u.y-b.p_z.
Classify the positive fibers as follows:

- I: a proper cap, with positive captured and residual d-volumes;
- E: zero captured volume and t_z=max_(x in C_z)u.x;
- F: full captured volume and t_z=min_(x in C_z)u.x.

The remaining zero or full captures have strict support gaps and
contribute zero to sufficiently small tilt variations. Let sigma_z
be H_(d-1)(C_z intersect {u.x=t_z}) for z in I,E,F. This is positive
for I; it may vanish at a supporting face in E or F. Define the
finite vector and two actual zonotopes in R^n by

    v = sum_(z in I) sigma_z p_z,
    Z_E = sum_(z in E) [0,sigma_z p_z],
    Z_F = sum_(z in F) [0,sigma_z p_z].

Then local criticality implies the set containment

    -Z_F subset v+Z_E.                              (1)

## Proof

For any beta in R^n, perturb b to b+epsilon*beta, epsilon>0.
At a proper cap the directional derivative is
sigma_z*(beta.p_z)/||u||. At an empty supporting cap it is
sigma_z*[beta.p_z]_+/||u|| by the support-face lemma. At a full
supporting cap, apply that lemma to the discarded side: the derivative
is -sigma_z*[-beta.p_z]_+/||u||. Facet boundaries themselves have
zero d-volume; using either strict or closed complements does not
change this derivative. There are finitely many fibers, so the
derivative of their sum is the sum of these derivatives.

Multiplying by ||u||, nonnegativity of every directional derivative
is exactly

    beta.v + sum_E sigma_z*[beta.p_z]_+
        - sum_F sigma_z*[-beta.p_z]_+ >= 0.           (2)

The first two terms are the support function of v+Z_E at beta.
The last sum is the support function of -Z_F at beta. Inequality
(2) for all beta is equivalent to (1): containment implies the
support inequalities; conversely any point of -Z_F outside the
compact convex set v+Z_E has a strictly separating linear functional,
contradicting the corresponding support inequality. This proves (1).

## Consequences and limits

Since 0 belongs to -Z_F, (1) implies a balanced section-area equation

    v + sum_E theta_z*sigma_z*p_z = 0,
    0<=theta_z<=1.

The full containment is stronger than existence of this one balance.
Every point of the full-facet zonotope must have its own compensation
inside the translated empty-facet zonotope.

If E is empty or all its supporting faces have zero (d-1)-measure,
then (1) forces v=0 and Z_F={0}. Thus every full supporting facet
at a base different from z0 must also have zero (d-1)-measure in that
case. A positive full-facet kink cannot be ignored when imposing
proper-cut stationarity.

With no supporting facets on either side, (1) reduces to the usual
proper-section base-barycenter equation v=0. For a proper A cut at
base -1 and an empty supporting B cut at base 1, with the source at
0, it gives the exact capacity condition sigma_A<=sigma_B.

Taking widths of (1) in both opposite directions also gives, for every
beta,

    sum_F sigma_z*|beta.p_z| <= sum_E sigma_z*|beta.p_z|.

This necessary directional section-capacity domination forgets the
translation v and is weaker than the original containment. Likewise,
if W is the linear span of the positive-capacity empty-facet vectors,
then v belongs to W and every positive-capacity full-facet vector
belongs to W. Indeed 0 in -Z_F first forces v in W; then every segment
of -Z_F is contained in v+Z_E subset W. These are exact consequences
of the actual integer tilt variations, not new assumptions about the
lattice bases or a sufficient condition for criticality.

Only the integer-normal projection is represented by these finite
zonotopes. Continuous-normal variations retain integrals of positive
parts of affine functions across each support facet, as in the
companion note; replacing those integrals by one freely chosen facet
centroid is not justified. Nor does (1) imply local minimality or
global depth criticality in the reverse direction.
